newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Shanghai newspapers - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Shanghai newspapers - May 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major political and business stories in local newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Shanghai. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- SHANGHAI SECURITIES NEWS - China has set the quota for new stock issues in 1997 at 30 billion yuan, compared with the 1996 quota of 15 billion, in a bid to support key state-run companies and cool down stock trading.

- The total number of stock trading accounts on the Shanghai stock exchange has hit 14.62 million, up 21 percent from the end of 1996, prompting stock exchange officials to warn new investors about risk.
- Major cities in China have taken measures to cool the current share-buying frenzy in response to the government's call to make 1997 the year of risk control for the securities markets.
- BUSINESS NEWS - The Shanghai computer industry is aiming for sales valued at nine billion yuan in 1997, an increase of nearly 50 percent against last year's 6.15 billion.
- Economic and trade cooperation between China and France has great potential, said a commentary issued ahead of a visit to Shanghai by French President Jacques Chirac on Saturday.
